Discuss a current medical ethics issues.
Talk about a time you had to make an ethical decision.
Is it ethical to treat your family members? Would you do it?
If a patient has AIDS, will you still treat them?
You have diagnosed a patient with HIV, and they do not want to tell their partner. What do you do?
What would you do if you diagnose a patient with syphilis, but he doesn't plan to tell his girlfriend?
You are a PA. Your collaborating MD asks you to administer a medication to a patient. You do not agree with his decision and feel it could harm the patient. What do you do?
You see a co-worker taking medication from the dispense cart and putting it in her bag. What do you do?
If you found out a classmate had old copies of exams, what would you do?
You are in a surgery and the anesthesiologist begins to make inappropriate comments about the patient once they are asleep. What do you do in this situation?
You're in an OR and have suspicions that the surgeon may be intoxicated. What do you do?

You have an elderly patient who needs to stay at the hospital for overnight observation. The patient is refusing, but the patient's son states the patient has dementia and is incapable of making medical decisions. The patient's son wants the patient admitted. What do you do?
You are leaving for the day and realize you gave a patient medication they are allergic to. What do you do?
A patient comes in for follow-up and you realize they were prescribed the wrong medication, but one with a similar name. What do you do?
You are working as a PA. You realize your nurse sent in the wrong medication for a patient. What do you do?
You realize you sent an adult dosage of medication for a child. What do you do?
You've prescribed an antibiotic, but after the patient leaves you realize there's a contraindication with one of their other medications. What do you do?
A patient calls back for their culture results, and you realize the test was never sent in. The sample is no longer good. What do you do?
When is honesty not the best policy?
You are seeing a Jehovah's Witness patient. Due to religious beliefs, he/she does not accept blood transfusions, but it could be life-saving. What do you do?

A child is brought in with injuries from falling out of a tree at a friend's house. His parents are out of town. After evaluation, it is determined that he requires a blood transfusion. Before giving the transfusion, you find a card in his pocket stating he is Jehovah's Witness and to not give blood transfusions. The procedure would save his life, but no parents are present. What do you do?
You are a PA and you prescribed birth control pills for a 13-year-old. The patient's mother is angry about this decision. What do you say?
What would you do if you hit your neighbor's dog?
What would you do if you hit a car in a parking lot? You're unsure of the owner.

If you were a color, what color would you be, and why?

Help this student complete the following task...
Give directions for putting on a pair of gloves.
Give instructions for making a peanut butter and jelly sandwich.
While sitting back to back, tell the person in the room how to draw a tree.
Explain how to make a paper airplane.
Help the patient in the room fill out their intake form. (Once in the room, you find that the patient is homeless, cannot read, and does not know much of the information.)
Interpret the graph displayed in the room.
Enter the room and perform the following calculations...
Convert the medication amount from milligrams to grams.
Discuss a pastime outside of school and how the skills acquired will help in your career.
If you could have any other job, besides being a PA or working in the medical field, what would you do?

What do you enjoy outside of work and school?

What are the 3 most important aspects in evaluating a PA program? What about a PA student?
What can our faculty do for you?
What accommodations will you need to successfully complete this program?
If you could do anything else and know you would be successful, what would you do?
Discuss a time you had to resolve a conflict.
Tell me about a time you worked with someone you didn't like.

Talk about a time you had to disagree with someone to get a positive outcome.
What are you famous for?
What are you well known for?
Why do people recognize you?

You discover a classmate is romantically involved with her preceptor. What should be done, if anything? Enter the room and discuss your position.
What would you do if you saw a classmate cheating on an exam?

A friend in your class confides in you that his mother was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. He is overwhelmed and may drop out of school to spend time with his mother. How do you counsel your friend?
You are a dermatology PA. A patient states they are out of opioid pain medication and unable to get more from their pain management physician for another few weeks. What do you do?

You are seeing a patient who is a gymnast and currently training for the Olympics. The patient's mother is upset because the patient recently gained 3 pounds. Enter the room and address this situation.
A boat is sinking. There is a lifeboat for one person. The passengers include a 75-year-old physician, 50-year-old army officer, 24-year-old teacher, and a 6-year old. Who gets the spot?
Tell me about a time you had to take a step back.
What leads your moral compass?
What drives you in your decisions?
If you were a car sitting on a car lot, how would you sell yourself?
